findings.claim: ADOPT-001 contains four stale locations that will actively misdirect adopters after 020H.2 merges. §12.7.13 still reads 'SHA256 verification is NOT yet wired for Regal at v1.0.0' and concludes with 'Adopters who want to harden the supply-chain posture before 020H.2 ships can fork the SCP repo…' — both clauses become false the moment this PR merges. §12.7.1 (line 794) still warns deployers to 'review §12.7.13 for the v1.0.0 supply-chain posture, including the known Regal SHA256 verification gap (TF-020H3-001)' — directing every new adopter to a gap that no longer exists. §12.7.9 still says '(Note: the CI workflow's Regal binary is NOT yet SHA256-verified — see §12.7.13 for the supply-chain disclosure)' — false post-merge. ADOPT-001 is absent from the DISPATCH-NOTE Files list and from the PR diff, despite STATUS.md's 020H.2 backlog description reading 'closes TF-020H3-001 (ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 supply-chain disclosure)' — which implies the doc update was intended in scope.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 (line 1033): 'SHA256 verification is NOT yet wired for Regal at v1.0.0 (lockfile + tool-versions parity with OPA + Conftest is tracked as TF-020H3-001 → slice 020H.2)'; §12.7.13 (line 1035): 'Adopters who want to harden the supply-chain posture before 020H.2 ships can fork the SCP repo, add Regal SHA256 verification…'; §12.7.1 (line 794): 'including the known Regal SHA256 verification gap (TF-020H3-001)'; §12.7.9 (line ~998): 'the CI workflow's Regal binary is NOT yet SHA256-verified — see §12.7.13'; DISPATCH-NOTE Files list (five entries — no ADOPT-001); STATUS.md 020H.2 backlog row: 'closes TF-020H3-001 (ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 supply-chain disclosure)'. The implementation is fully correct: scripts/.tool-versions has 'regal 0.40.0', scp-policy-check.lock has all four platform SHA256 entries, and resolve_regal() in policy-check.yml SHA256-verifies before cp then smoke-tests post-copy. The gap is documentation-only — but it is an actively misleading false negative directed at every adopter reading §12.7.
findings.impact: Every adopter who reads ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 after 020H.2 merges is told the Regal SHA256 gap is still open and that they should fork SCP to harden it. §12.7.1 sends deployers to §12.7.13 to review 'the known Regal SHA256 verification gap' — this creates unnecessary fork-and-maintain work for security-conscious adopters who cannot distinguish 'stale pre-020H.2 disclosure text' from 'gap still live.' The estate-cascade adopters (FLA, PIM, recommender, shopify-app, mapp-doc-agent, control-tower per WP-SCP-024) will all encounter this misdirection when they read the integration guide. The supply-chain disclosure section's purpose was to give adopters accurate posture; post-020H.2-merge it gives inaccurate posture in the negative direction (claiming a gap that doesn't exist).
findings.mitigation: Either (A) include ADOPT-001 diff in this PR: update §12.7.13 to read that Regal SHA256 verification IS wired in 020H.2 (PR # + commit SHA once known), remove the fork-guidance paragraph, update §12.7.1 to remove the TF-020H3-001 gap reference, and update §12.7.9 to drop the 'NOT yet SHA256-verified' parenthetical; OR (B) if ADOPT-001 update is deferred to a follow-up doc PR, create an explicit TF-020H2-001 entry in STATUS.md with: closure path = standalone doc PR updating all four stale §12.7 locations, named carrier slice (020H.1 or SCP-073.sec whichever opens first), and a hard deadline (before v1.0.1 or within 14 calendar days of 020H.2 merge — same cadence pattern as TF-020H3-001 itself). Option (A) is cleaner and closes TF-020H3-001 cleanly. Option (B) requires the TF-020H2-001 entry to land in this PR's STATUS.md diff.

findings.claim: TF-007 text in STATUS.md covers OPA Sigstore only; the DISPATCH-NOTE claims Regal Sigstore 'folds into TF-007' but TF-007's authoritative text does not name Regal. This leaves the Regal Sigstore closure path undocumented in the source-of-truth.
findings.evidence: STATUS.md tracked-forward items from 020C.1 (line 89): 'TF-007: re-tighten `gh attestation verify` to hard-fail when OPA upstream begins publishing Sigstore attestations.' — names OPA only. DISPATCH-NOTE 020h2 'Out-of-scope' section: 'Not adding the soft-warn here keeps the slice minimal; folds into TF-007.' The claim is valid in intent (OPA and Regal share the same upstream attestation gap and the same re-tighten moment) but TF-007 as written would be considered closed by OPA attestation publication alone, silently leaving Regal without a tracked path.
findings.impact: If a future maintainer resolves TF-007 for OPA only (OPA v1.x begins publishing attestations before Regal does), they could mark TF-007 closed without adding the soft-warn for Regal. findings.mitigation: Amend TF-007 text in STATUS.md to read: 're-tighten `gh attestation verify` to hard-fail when OPA upstream begins publishing Sigstore attestations; also wire Regal Sigstore soft-warn (deferred from 020H.2 to keep slice minimal — both tools likely share the same upstream gap timeline).' Alternatively, create TF-020H2-001 specifically for Regal Sigstore with a closure path referencing TF-007's resolution as the trigger. Either option must land in this PR's STATUS.md diff.

The DISPATCH-NOTE documents this as 'SHA256 verification was performed inside resolve_regal against the lockfile pin' — which is accurate — but a reader comparing the SAFE-011 mitigation text to the implementation will find the literal prescription not followed.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml resolve_regal() calls verify_sha256 on '${RUNNER_TEMP}/${REGAL_ASSET}' then returns the path; the caller does 'cp ${REGAL_SOURCE} ${BIN_DIR}/regal; chmod +x; ${BIN_DIR}/regal version'. No second verify_sha256 on '${BIN_DIR}/regal'. SAFE-011 mitigation: 'Add a verify_sha256 "${BIN_DIR}/regal" "${REGAL_SHA256}"'. OPA follows the same pattern as Regal (verify inside resolve_opa before cp); Conftest has a second post-extraction verify because archive SHA ≠ extracted-binary SHA.
